sec-oncall: Security advisory (P2): possible misuse of a PyPI API token used to publish private packages. Token was found in a third-party CI log we consume for integration tests. No public package tampering detected, but we need an org-wide action to harden publishing and rotate tokens.
sec-oncall: Immediate required actions for package owners: 1) Revoke and rotate any PyPI tokens used by CI or corp automation that have publish scope. 2) Lock down repository publish permissions to an allowlist of service accounts. 3) Temporarily disable automated publishes from external CI providers. 4) Audit recent publishes to our private index for unexpected versions or tarball changes.
pkg-admin: confirmed initial finding: token for user `ci-publisher@redwood` appeared in logs ingested from vendor CI job `vendor-int-tests/runner-7` at 2026-03-24T11:12Z. Token had full `:owner` and `:publish` scopes on the private PyPI index (`pypi.redwood.internal`).
pypi-bot: automated alert: checksum mismatch detected for package `@redwood/cli` version 1.12.3 in internal index vs upstream checksum recorded at publish time. Flagging for manual review.
alice: ack. Which packages to check first? I can start with internal libs and the CLI packages.
sec-oncall: priority list: @redwood/cli, @redwood/sdk-py, @redwood/utils-py, and any packages published in the last 48 hours. Treat all publishes from ci-publisher as suspect.
bob: rotating the ci-publisher token now. New token will be minted and stored in Vault under secret/pypi/ci-publisher-20260324. I'll remove publish scope from any fallback tokens.
infra: pausing external CI-triggered publishes: toggled `allow_external_publishes=false` in the PyPI proxy config and paused webhooks from vendor CI providers.
devrel: notifying integrators and internal devs: temporary manual publish flow required while we confirm integrity. We'll share instructions for using the new Vault token.
qa: starting package integrity checks: re-downloading tarballs for the last 72 hours and verifying checksums, signing status, and wheel metadata. I'll post any anomalies here.
sec-oncall: commands/notes for owners: - List tokens in Vault: `vault list secret/pypi` - Revoke token in PyPI service: `pypictl tokens revoke --id <token-id>` - Rotate token: `pypictl tokens create --name ci-publisher --scopes "read,upload" --out /tmp/new && vault kv put secret/pypi/ci-publisher token=@/tmp/new`
alice: running audit: `pypictl list-packages --since 2026-03-22T00:00Z --filter publisher=ci-publisher | jq .` and bulk-verify checksums with `sha256sum -c checksums.txt`.
bob: rotation done. Old token revoked (id=tp-7812), new token stored at `secret/pypi/ci-publisher-20260324` with limited scopes (upload only to allowlist projects). Note: removed owner privileges from the CI role.
infra: publishing pipeline now requires a Vault-backed token and will validate package signature against our keyring: added step `verify-signature` to publishing workflow. PR infra/pypi#314.
pypi-bot: manual review: found one suspicious publish for @redwood/cli 1.12.3 with mismatched checksum. That artifact has been quarantined and flagged for rollback.
devrel: informing partners: we will block new installs of quarantined versions and advise to pin to 1.12.2 until we confirm.
qa: integrity scan results so far: 7 packages within window had matching checksums; 1 package (@redwood/cli 1.12.3) mismatch. Extracting tarball for manual inspection now.
legal: capture audit trail and who had access to the vendor logs where token was found. We may need to notify affected customers if we determine tampering reached downstream releases.
sec-oncall: secondary actions: 1) Add pre-publish DLP gate that rejects tokens embedded in build logs/artifacts. 2) Add mandatory package signatures for internal index (cosign or GPG). 3) Enforce allowlist publish permissions per-package. 4) Add an org-wide policy: no long-lived publish tokens; require rotation every 30 days and Vault storage.
alice: I'll open infra PRs: one to add signature verification in the publish pipeline, another to add the Vault token reference enforcement and DLP pre-check.
bob: listing recent publishes from ci-publisher: `pypictl list-publishes --publisher ci-publisher --since 2026-03-23T00:00Z` returned 4 publishes; quarantined the CLI artifact and rolled back the index entry for 1.12.3.
infra: toggled enforcement rules in the internal index: automatic rollback for mismatched checksum publishes enabled, external webhooks blocked for publish events until further notice.\nsec-oncall: containment summary: token revoked, new token minted with reduced scope and stored in Vault, external publishes paused, suspicious artifact quarantined, integrity audit in progress. Owners: please complete rotations and validations within 4h. Postmortem and exec summary will follow.
qa: found that the mismatched CLI tarball contains an extra top-level `scripts/` file that wasn't present in 1.12.2. Forensics team, please advise if this warrants a deeper code review.
sec-oncall: forensics assigned: bob + pkg-admin. If you find anything that indicates malicious injection, escalate to incident channel and legal.
devrel: temporary notice for internal docs: "Publishing is suspended for external CI providers. Use Vault-stored token and follow signed-publish flow."
legal: preserving all evidence and audit logs. I'll coordinate the notification timeline with sec-oncall if customer-facing impact is found.
sec-oncall: thanks all. Keep this thread updated with verification results. We'll publish a short exec note after the audit completes. :lock:
